purpose: Evidence bank for original Guanxi culture lessons. Facts are paraphrased; source pages are not copied.
editorial_rules: Separate observed local facts from the fictional cast’s choices.
Teach clarification instead of mind-reading; a hesitant answer can reflect uncertainty, timing or refusal.
Stereotyped nationality questions are not valid learner assessments. Frame choices around the specific situation.
A polite refusal of alcohol or disclosure of dietary requirements is always an available response.
Source codes support only listed facts, not every teaching recommendation. Original scenario advice should be identified as such.
Do not turn cultural knowledge into claims that contracts, verification or boundaries are unnecessary.
Verify time-sensitive travel and payment procedures at the time of use; the course should focus on language for asking.

sources.title: Huaqiangbei electronics street
sources.publisher: Shenzhen Municipal Talent Affairs Bureau / EyeShenzhen
sources.verification: web search result and/or opened source read; only the limited claims below are supported
supported_claims: Huaqiangbei is an electronics-market district in Futian, with markets spanning electronic components and finished products.
The area also includes food and non-electronics shopping.
sources.authoring_notes: Use as the setting for comparing sample specifications, quantities and supplier details. Do not infer every stall owns a factory or that cheap means equivalent quality.

sources.title: City upgrades 3 intangible cultural heritages to municipal level
sources.verification: web search result and/or opened source read; only the limited claims below are supported
supported_claims: Kuichong Hakka chaguo and Nan’ao sea-urchin zongzi are documented local food traditions of Dapeng.
Hakka chaguo is also called ban in Hakka.
sources.authoring_notes: Use to counter the claim that Shenzhen has no history or local food. Do not give Hakka words as though they are Mandarin pronunciations.

sources.title: Time-honored restaurants for enjoying morning tea in GZ
sources.verification: web search result and/or opened source read; only the limited claims below are supported
supported_claims: Guangzhou has a documented morning-tea restaurant tradition; Tao Tao Ju and Lian Xiang Lou are examples.
Teahouses carry local culinary history and social significance.
sources.authoring_notes: Use a Guangzhou breakfast meeting as a setting, with asking what to order and inviting recommendations. Do not claim all Cantonese people breakfast this way or that tea etiquette is uniform.

sources.title: Business etiquette in China
sources.verification: web search result and/or opened source read; only the limited claims below are supported
supported_claims: The guide emphasizes developing relationships, following personal introductions, patience and courteous meetings.
The guide discusses handling business cards, hosting and rank in formal settings.
sources.authoring_notes: Guidance is general and not a personality test. Teach asking preferred names/titles, following the host and confirming details. Gift and banquet customs do not override consent, company policy or written commercial checks.

sources.title: Cross-border Spending
sources.verification: web search result and/or opened source read; only the limited claims below are supported
supported_claims: International visitors can link supported international cards to Weixin Pay for supported merchant payments.
The provider documents QR payment and in-app payment flows.
sources.authoring_notes: Eligibility, fees and limits can change; link the live provider guide and avoid fixed figures. Merchant payment is not a promise of person-to-person transfer or red-envelope access.

sources.title: 12306 FAQ
sources.verification: web search result and/or opened source read; only the limited claims below are supported
supported_claims: The English site supports valid foreign passports for real-name booking.
Passengers use the ID associated with the ticket for travel; an itinerary or reimbursement receipt is not itself a ticket.
sources.authoring_notes: Use station names and matching passport details in dialogue. Avoid invented departure times, ticket prices or universal assumptions about automatic gates.

sources.title: The Nanshan District you cannot miss: Historical sites
sources.verification: web search result and/or opened source read; only the limited claims below are supported
supported_claims: Nantou Ancient Town was an administrative and trade center long before modern Shenzhen’s special-economic-zone development.
Shekou has historic neighborhoods; the Chiwan Tianhou Temple honors Mazu.
sources.authoring_notes: Use a weekend invitation to Nantou or Shekou to connect historical and modern Shenzhen. Do not repeat dubious etymologies as fact; the snake story is explicitly folklore.

sources.title: Shekou Subdistrict
sources.verification: web search result and/or opened source read; only the limited claims below are supported
supported_claims: Shekou is part of Nanshan, facing Hong Kong across Shenzhen Bay.
The government profile describes a mixture of registered, non-registered and international residents.
sources.authoring_notes: Use geographic context, not old population totals as current statistics. Never generalize Shekou’s international scene to all Shenzhen neighborhoods.

sources.title: Spring festival, social practices of the Chinese people in celebration of traditional new year
sources.verification: Full indexed entry text returned by web search was read; direct open returned a JavaScript/CAPTCHA challenge. No challenge bypassed.
supported_claims: The festival includes preparations, family reunion meals and greetings to relatives, friends and neighbors.
Traditions are transmitted within families and communities and vary in expression.
sources.authoring_notes: Teach asking a colleague about their own holiday plans and agreeing project availability in advance. Do not assume every person goes home or give unverified statutory closure dates.

sources.title: Traditional tea processing techniques and associated social practices in China
sources.verification: Full indexed entry text returned by web search was read.
supported_claims: Tea drinking and sharing occur in homes, workplaces and teahouses and can support hospitality and social relationships.
Tea production and social practices differ by locality and community.
sources.authoring_notes: A tea invitation is a context for curiosity and conversation, not evidence a business agreement exists. Avoid attributing one drinking ritual to everyone.

sources.title: Steamed Meat Buns
sources.publisher: Shanghai Government / Shanghai Intangible Cultural Heritage Protection Centre
sources.verification: web search result and/or opened source read; only the limited claims below are supported
supported_claims: Shanghai’s Nanxiang tradition includes soup-filled buns called xiaolongbao in Mandarin and xiaolong mantou locally.
sources.authoring_notes: Use regional food terminology to show that familiar words can vary by place. Do not teach all mantou throughout China as filled buns.

sources.title: 来了深圳，都是一家人 | 创业篇
sources.verification: web search result and/or opened source read; only the limited claims below are supported
supported_claims: The city uses the slogan 来了就是深圳人 as part of its civic identity.
sources.authoring_notes: Label this as a civic slogan, not a legal-residency statement or proof that everyone experiences inclusion equally. A character can ask where a colleague grew up rather than assume their home province.

sources.title: China: Business Travel
supported_claims: The guide describes face-to-face meetings and trust as important to business development.
It documents both physical business cards and increasing WeChat contact exchange.
sources.authoring_notes: Use this as contemporary business context, not universal rules about individual Chinese people; do not repeat travel/legal guidance without separate checking.

sources.title: Dragon Boat festival
supported_claims: The festival begins on the fifth day of the fifth lunar month.
Practices and commemorated figures vary by region; rice dumplings and boat races are among documented traditions.
sources.authoring_notes: No fixed Gregorian date, no assumption that all employees celebrate alike; ask about family practice. Do not present traditional health beliefs as medical facts.

sources.title: Tone Sandhi
supported_claims: In a pair of third tones, the first is pronounced as a second tone while conventionally retaining its written third-tone mark.
一 and 不 have context-dependent spoken tone changes.
sources.authoring_notes: Course uses citation pinyin with separately labeled spoken forms. This beginner rule is not a complete algorithm for long third-tone sequences.

sources.title: Teahouse Leisure for Chengdu’s Autumn
supported_claims: Heming Teahouse is in Chengdu’s People’s Park and attracts local residents and visitors.
Daqi Teahouse occupies a converted lacquerware craft factory and includes a lacquerware exhibition upstairs.
Yuelai Tea Garden combines tea with Sichuan opera.
sources.authoring_notes: Teach different local spaces and invitations. Do not imply Chengdu residents all have one personality; avoid current hours or prices.

sources.title: The Chengdu teahouse and the good life
supported_claims: The author describes Chengdu teahouses as social spaces for conversation, games, reading and performances.
Teahouses vary in setting and formality, including neighborhood streets, parks and temples.
sources.authoring_notes: Use firsthand descriptions, not the author’s universalized conclusions about what an invitation means. No old prices or historical claims from secondary references.
